text.p: The merger of Sembawang Corp (SembCorp) and Jurong Shipyards Ltd (JSL) was finalised on Wednesday, Standard Chartered Merchant Bank Asia said.
It said in a statement all the conditions set out in a March 31 agreement to create one the the world's largest ship repair firms had been fulfilled.

"Accordingly, SembCorp has exercised on 23rd July 1997 the put option granted under the option agreement, pursuant to which JSL will acquire the shipyard operations of the SembCorp Group," the bankers said.
JSL would now isse 27.6 million new Singapore $0.50 shares to SembCorp at S$6.80 each for the assets SembCorp will inject into the merged firm, the statement said.
These include Sembawang Shipyard, Bohai Sembawang Shipyard in Tianjin, China and PT karimum Sembawang Shipyard in Indonesia, estimated to be worth S$187.4 million.
The moves resulted in SembCorp's stake in JSL rising to 38.6 percent from 23.4 percent and triggered a conditional takeover offer for all the rest of JSL's shares.
The statement said shareholders could take S$6.80 in cash per share or 500 new ordinary shares of S$1.00 each in SembCorp and S$3,400 in cash for every 1,000 offer shares.
